text:
maya: Heads-up — during the console walkthrough today a few folks pointed out the in-product docs panel uses different terms than the main docs. Quick thread to align before we ship the dashboard tweaks.

olivia_design: Noted. Examples?

maya: "Quick Actions" vs "Routes" — the help panel still says Quick Actions but the console UI calls them Routes. Also the docs refer to "tokens" in some places and "units" in others which confuses new users.

sam_docs: Oof. I saw at least three pages with "tokens"/"units" mismatch. One is the in-app embed doc that the helper panel surfaces.

olivia_design: Visual issue too — crosslinks from help panel open the doc in a modal that doesn't focus the first heading, so screen readers don't announce the new context. Accessibility flagged by audit.

raj_engineering: Technically the modal is reused across several panels; changing focus is easy. The tricky bit is stable anchor ids in the docs: some headings are auto-generated and have changed after last deploy. Those anchors break the deep links.

ben_prod: For consistency we should decide on canonical labels (e.g., use "Routes" everywhere). That will reduce confusion and analytics fragmentation. We can run a quick search for occurrences.

sam_docs: Proposal: accept canonical terms list and add a small redirect layer for old anchors. For example, if we used `#quick-actions` previously, map it to `#routes` server-side for links surfaced from the app.

olivia_design: Also propose we change the help panel copy to a short phrase + 1-line description, not full doc excerpts. Less likely to show stale terminology.

maya: Agreed on the smaller snippets. Can we also add an explicit "Open full docs" link (new tab) so we avoid modal focus problems?

raj_engineering: Adding the external open is trivial. For the modal, we should set `aria-modal="true"` and run `focus()` on the heading id after the modal mounts. I'll add that in the PR.

sam_docs: For anchors mapping, here's a tiny example we can include in the docs site config (we can make it a small JSON map):

```
{
  "quick-actions": "routes",
  "token-cost": "units-cost"
}
```

sam_docs: We'll also add a tiny banner at top of the doc page when an old anchor is used: "You were redirected from a legacy link — here's the canonical section." Keeps things clear for users and search.

ben_prod: Can we add an event for analytics when a redirect occurs? Want to see how many old links are hit.

raj_engineering: Yep, emit a `docs_deeplink_redirect` event with the original hash. Low overhead.

olivia_design: Accessibility follow-ups: make sure headings have skip links and that the help panel's link target is the first substantive heading (h2) not the tiny crumb. Also check color contrast on the small in-panel snippets (a11y flagged a contrast ratio ~3.9).

maya: Who owns what?

sam_docs: I can own the canonical terms list and update the docs. I'll add the redirect map and banner.

raj_engineering: I'll own the modal focus + analytics event + redirect mapping implementation on the docs site.

olivia_design: I'll update the help panel copy and validate color/accessibility.

ben_prod: I'll schedule a quick canary rollout for the help panel changes and wire up analytics.

maya: Sweet. Can we aim for PRs by EOD Friday? Also please @me on the PRs.

sam_docs: Yep — opening a draft PR now, will call out the canonical term list in the description.

deploy-bot: docs-site: PR #842 opened by sam_docs — "canonical-terms + deeplink map" (labels: docs, a11y).

maya: Perfect. After the canary we'll sanity-check the help panel links across a few tenant orgs (esp. private deploys). Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

olivia_design: Quick note — if we can't stabilize anchors quickly we'll fall back to linking to the top of the doc with a short anchorless preview and a CTA to search within the doc. Less ideal but safe.

sam_docs: Good fallback. I'll include that in the PR as an option guarded by a feature flag so we can revert if needed.

ben_prod: And I'll add a short entry to the release notes about terminology harmonization for customer-facing folks.

maya: Great. Closing the loop here. We'll reconvene after the canary metrics are in.
